_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 9 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_session: 231 (SkyReply) — two SkyView controls that were never broken, then the course outline planned on real welding data
_status: Two things you reported turned out to be working controls with nothing to show. The search box always could scroll; it was only ever asked for eight suggestions out of hundreds, so there was nothing below the fold — it now offers sixty, says when there are more, and the arrow keys carry the list with them. The Show menu was changing its label and its count while the map drew nothing, because individual courses are only drawn once you have zoomed in and SkyView opens further out than that; now a discipline with nothing switched on disappears, so Deselect all empties the map at the view it opens on. Testing the rest of the map afterwards found two more things nobody had reported: the published copy of SkyView was one edit out of date, and the fix itself had made a search pick able to land on a discipline that had just been filtered away. Then the course outline: on a double-click a course would open a panel with what the colleges report, a description and a list of skills the platform drafts from the member catalogs, all editable and waiting on a faculty reviewer. It is drawn as a working prototype on real data for Introduction to Welding and nothing is built into SkyView yet — you asked to see the plan first, and the prototype is where reacting is cheap.

items.text: The course outline prototype is here, drawn on the real Introduction to Welding record (24 colleges teach it): https://claude.ai/code/artifact/f04e8f30-8cf5-4731-9da7-849335d7102f — the title and description you can edit, fifteen skills each carrying how many of the 24 colleges' own catalog text supports it, what the colleges report to the Chancellor's Office with the spread shown (their units run from 0 to 5), the thirteen outline slots nothing we hold can fill, and a panel putting the academic skills beside the agency side. Everything the platform wrote carries your label, MAP-Generated for faculty consideration and revision before use. React to the shape and the wording; nothing is built into SkyView yet.

The one thing the outline cannot be built without: where agency skill statements come from. For welding we hold 64 classified credentials — American Welding Society 18, Carpenters Training Committee for Northern California 15, the colleges themselves 12, ASME 7, LA Building and Safety 4, NCCER 4, Iron Workers 3 — and 57 published credit recommendations against them. Not one of them says what a holder can DO; they say where credit lands. So the agency half of the comparison has to come from the standards themselves. Published standards, ACE exhibits, or someone keying them in? And which certification should be the first one examined end to end — the unit of work is one certification, not one discipline.

Build the outline into SkyView as a layered panel (exhibits and military credit recommendations are the next layers). Edits go to kb_curation, which already carries unified_title, discipline and canonical_subj4; validated_at and validated_by exist there and have never been used on any of the 34,000 rows, so this is their first real use. A subject change re-keys the identity, so it queues and waits for verification plus admin release. Double-click is currently taken by the discipline work surface — split it, a course opens the outline and empty ground keeps today's behavior. Add a Beginning/Intermediate/Advanced level to the course and to each skill, seeded where the text already says so and left for a curator where it does not; keep course level and skill level as separate fields.

The evaluation runs certification to courses, not the other way round: one certification examined for which course or courses it aligns with ENOUGH for credit. The outline as prototyped is course-first, which makes it the destination of an evaluation rather than its entry point — a certification-first view is a first-class screen, not a later convenience. The test every screen has to pass is Sam's: would a faculty member want this person to have to take their class when they already know this stuff.

The memory audit sheet takes your replies on the page now: https://claude.ai/code/artifact/a233dd0c-d5ad-40e9-b85a-bae8f9f05217 (kept in the repo as docs/visuals/2026-09-05-memory-audit-verdicts.html). Under each of the 43 items, each of the 76 memories listed inside items 2 and 3, and the 31 retired rows: a row of reply chips (Yes takes the recommendation; under a memory the first chip names the action, Verify or Retire), a Follow up toggle for anything you want the session to come back to whatever the verdict, and a note for what a word cannot carry. The line under each reply says what was saved. Your replies save to the sheet itself; the next session reads them from there. Item 1 is the one large call, the 352 entries that passed with evidence.

Read Sam's replies from the sheet's store first (Artifact read_db, collection replies: item, ref, verdict, note, follow-up; a verdict of yes on a memory, saved before the relabel, is the batch's recommendation for it, and Sam's in-chat replies of 2026-09-05 on the Board amendment and the $1 million noncredit memories count too), then execute them from kb/memory_audit/2026-09-05-receipt.json: the held promotions first, then the human-sourced rows he rules on, then the hygiene fixes; every item flagged Follow up goes on this feed with his note. One guarded statement per batch, keyed on id, one log row per change, never delegated. Then re-run the memory lint and update the lane file's counts.

Three things the audit noticed outside the memory rows need a look: the nightly cleanup worklist has silently lost its P1 and P5 classes because the text they key on matches nothing on the nightly-loaded table; the student-detail lane file still quotes the figures from before the nightly load replaced the table; and the spelling lint sees only about 8% of CLAUDE.md because its code-fence mask runs to the end of the file.

Watch Sam's reaction to the By subject table's standing column. Every row that reads “not X’s code” is either a stray the prefix fold missed or an umbrella code the seed does not know about; if he wants it as a worklist, fold-verify is the planner of record, not a new one.

Five COBI tabs still scroll sideways on a phone — the Dashboard worst, by 887 pixels, then RACI, Budget, Memory and Activities. That is the plainest of the accessibility findings and the one a person actually feels. Several sit in sections the daily rebuild owns, so the fix is in the generator, not the page.

One colour decision unblocks an accessibility fix across the whole suite. Roughly four thousand “no value here” markers (the italic “— no articulations” in the grids) are currently too faint to read — 2.34:1 against a 4.5:1 standard. Making them the normal muted grey would fix it but make absence the loudest thing on a dense screen, which is backwards. The proposal is a new quiet grey (#6B6B66) that just clears the standard and stays the quietest thing in the row. Say yes, or say use the normal muted grey.

The accessibility sweep now runs as one command — `npm run a11y` — over all 42 views in about 100 seconds, and COBI's 38 tabs are found from the side menu itself, so a new tab is checked the day it ships. The problems shared by every view are fixed: the side menu group headings and the signed-out line were too faint to read, three controls were under the minimum tap size, the painting fallback panel failed on its own background, and nothing in COBI respected a reader's request to stop moving things. What is left is per-tab and named: five tabs still scroll sideways on a phone (the Dashboard worst, by 887 pixels), eighteen carry text below the contrast standard, and four thousand small tap targets come from just fifty-four rules — one button in the Credential Reference grid accounts for over two thousand of them. Start with the sideways scroll.

Sam approved moving baked-in configuration into tables. Two to start: the list of sites in cobi_orgs.js (adding or renaming a site is currently a code deploy) and the alpha banner's wording. public.cobi_nav is the precedent for the first, the sierra_guidance row for the second.
